headline: PALADIN HITS 4.25% U3O8 AT NEW ATLAS DISCOVERY 3.5KM FROM TRIPLE R — 7 OF 8 HOLES MINERALIZED AT PATTERSON LAKE SOUTH (PDN)
snippet: Paladin Energy (ASX:PDN, TSX:PDN) announced June 25 the discovery of the Atlas uranium body at its Patterson Lake South project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin — 3.5km south of the high-grade Triple R deposit and 4.5km southwest of last year's Saloon East discovery — with 7 of 8 winter drill holes intersecting significant uranium mineralisation across 2,408 total metres. Discovery hole PLS26-708B returned 8.0m averaging 1.75% U3O8, including 3.0m at 4.25% U3O8 from 190m depth. Atlas remains open along strike and at depth and is a primary target for the 2026 summer drill program — adding a third spatial cluster to an increasingly district-scale system at one of the world's premier undeveloped uranium projects.

headline: COPPER SURGES 2.1% OFF 7-WEEK LOWS AS JUNE 30 TARIFF DECISION LOOMS — GRASBERG AT 40-50% CAPACITY AFTER FATAL LANDSLIDE
snippet: Copper futures staged a forceful 2.1% recovery on June 26 off their lowest levels in seven weeks — LME near $13,000/tonne, CME near $5.99/lb — as markets rebalanced ahead of the June 30 U.S. Commerce Department Section 232 report that will determine whether a phased 15–30% tariff on refined copper imports proceeds in 2027. Supply fundamentals underpinned the rebound: Freeport-McMoRan's Grasberg Block Cave in Indonesia remains at 40–50% of nameplate capacity following last September's fatal landslide, while Kamoa-Kakula continues to face acid supply constraints. Goldman Sachs holds a 600,000-tonne refined copper deficit forecast for 2026 — the largest in over two decades.

headline: OMAI DRILLS 7.26 g/t GOLD OVER 34.8m AT WENOT — PEA 4-6 WEEKS OUT, 93% CIL RECOVERY CONFIRMED (TSXV:OMG)
snippet: Omai Gold Mines (TSXV:OMG) released June 24 assays from six holes in its ongoing 50,000m drilling program at the Omai Gold Project in Guyana, with standout hole 26ODD-185 returning 7.26 g/t gold over 34.8m at central Wenot — the highest-grade bulk intercept from 58 holes (27,770m) completed so far in 2026. The company simultaneously confirmed Phase 1 metallurgical results of 93–95% gold recovery via standard CIL, removing processing uncertainty from a deposit already heading into a Preliminary Economic Assessment (PEA) expected in 4–6 weeks. A deep hole at the Gilt Deposit has reached 742m and continues, adding potential for a second high-grade underground resource zone.

headline: SAGA METALS CONSOLIDATES 72,107-HA JAMES BAY LITHIUM BLOCK AS SPODUMENE RALLIES ABOVE $2,000/T (CSE:SAGA)
snippet: SAGA Metals Corp. (CSE:SAGA) announced June 24 the formal consolidation of its Legacy and Amirault Lithium projects into a single 72,107-hectare (178,181-acre) block in Quebec's James Bay region — recovering full control after the expiry of a Rio Tinto JV — with field work returning encouraging LCT pegmatite indicators across the consolidated southern claims. The consolidation comes as spodumene concentrate (6% Li2O) has rebounded above US$2,000/t after collapsing to $760/t in 2023–2024, and as a 342 km² aeromagnetic dataset (7,132 line-km) gathered during the JV period identifies multiple untested magnetic anomalies warranting drill follow-up in one of Quebec's most active lithium exploration districts.

headline: GOLD HUNTER FIRES UP INAUGURAL 10,000m AT GREAT NORTHERN NEWFOUNDLAND — THOR DEPOSIT, VIKING BLOCK ON FIRST DRILL LIST (CSE:HUNT)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Gold Hunter Resources Inc. (CSE:HUNT)
snippet: Gold Hunter Resources (CSE:HUNT) confirmed June 25 the commencement of its first-ever diamond drill program at the 26,237-hectare Great Northern Project in Newfoundland — targeting up to 10,000 metres with MCL Drilling across three concurrent target styles: on-trend extension drilling at the Thor Deposit and Viking Block, historical resource verification at the Rattling Brook estimate, and regional exploration along the 10km gold-bearing structural corridor of the Doucers Valley Fault. Equity Exploration Consultants is managing all exploration activities on a consolidated land package that covers multiple styles of gold mineralisation in an established Atlantic Canadian camp with existing road access and infrastructure.

headline: ING SLASHES 2026 GOLD OUTLOOK — Q3 CUT TO $4,300 FROM $4,850, Q4 TO $4,600 FROM $5,000 ON DOLLAR SURGE AND YIELD SPIKE
snippet: ING Research downgraded its full-year gold price targets on June 24, cutting Q3 2026 to $4,300/oz from $4,850 and Q4 to $4,600/oz from $5,000 — among the largest single-revision forecast cuts by a bulge-bracket bank this correction cycle — citing the dollar climbing to its highest level in over a year and real yields rising as the Fed's June dot plot lifted the median year-end rate to 3.8% with median 2026 PCE inflation revised up to 3.6%. Even with the haircut, ING's revised targets sit 7–15% above current spot, a signal the bank views the correction as cyclical rather than structural; silver targets were also reduced in line with the gold move.

headline: ADAM HAMILTON: GOLD'S SUMMER DOLDRUMS ARE THE SETUP — 2026'S JUNE LULL IS "QUITE BULLISH" FOR AUTUMN RALLY
snippet: In his annual late-June seasonal piece, Zeal LLC's Adam Hamilton argues that gold's 2026 summer doldrums — the metal's weakest window of the year, historically concentrated in June and early July — carry the most bullish setup in years: gold has corrected to its least-overbought readings since early in the bull market, dramatically reducing the probability of a significant additional selloff while setting up a stronger-than-average autumn rally. Hamilton frames the June weakness as the optimal accumulation window before the sequential seasonal upturn that historically launches gold's largest quarterly gains, and notes that this year's dip is occurring against an unchanged structural demand backdrop of 1,000+ tonnes annual central bank buying.

headline: SILVER'S SIXTH SUPPLY DEFICIT + 67:1 GOLD RATIO — WHY JUNE 2026'S CORRECTION IS THE SETUP, NOT THE PEAK
snippet: A June 2026 analysis from GoldSilver.com frames silver's 53% collapse from January's $121.62 all-time high not as trend reversal but as an accumulation setup: the global silver market is heading for its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces, a figure unchanged by Fed rate signalling; the gold-silver ratio stretched to 67:1 is at its widest since the January Iran conflict peak and historically has presaged silver's largest percentage outperformance in the subsequent rally; and Bank of America's three-hike 2026 forecast — the most aggressive on the street — is now the priced-in consensus worst case, leaving limited downside surprise risk from rates alone.
